headline: Piscataqua-Salmon Falls and Winnipesaukee River dominate tonight's avian-influenza wildlife susceptibility hotspots, with Lower Minnesota and Pamlico Sound trailing at roughly half their scores.
hotspots: Piscataqua-Salmon Falls (MA, ME, NH) — score 1.000, n=258
methods_note: Wildlife susceptibility was modeled with xnicher ellipsoid models fitted to ERA5 bioclimatic normals using 95 percent ecoregions as the accessible area and APHIS wild-bird detections rasterized with a 1/120-degree recency kernel aggregated to HUC8 watersheds.
watchlist: Marine mammals Eubalaena glacialis and Balaenoptera borealis were fitted on terrestrial bioclimatic variables with low marine fractions, making their accessible-area and background assumptions implausible.

Several sparse species with n below 60 — including Rhynchopsitta terrisi, Sciurus alleni, Charadrius nivosus, Urocyon littoralis, and Pterodroma feae — show near-universal acceptance and unstable ellipsoids, warranting System-2 review of accessible area, background, and small-sample validity.
